source.title: Towards mechanistic understanding in a data-driven weather model: internal activations reveal interpretable physical features

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses feature splitting as a possible explanation for probe performance but does not measure whether larger-dictionary features replace smaller ones, partition their inputs, or lie near their directions.
record.gate_note: Appendix E reports single-feature probe performance over SAE hyperparameters and speculates that feature splitting could explain why intermediate-sized dictionaries perform best for tropical-cyclone detection. This does not test the splitting properties named in the claim versions. Figure 9 contains probe-score plots; the text gives no exact scores for the size sweep.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs on GraphCast layer 8 across dictionary sizes and reports single-feature tropical-cyclone probe F1. It invokes feature splitting only as a hypothesis for why intermediate sizes do best. It never matches features across sizes, checks input coverage or direction, or examines hierarchy or absorption, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors hypothesize that feature splitting (e.g., separate hurricane and typhoon features) explains why intermediate-sized SAEs give the best TC probes. They do not test this. They also report no clear size trend for ARs.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains k-sparse SAEs and evaluates single-feature probes across latent dimensions; it does not apply a method for matching or comparing features across dictionary sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: Tropical-cyclone probe performance varies with SAE hyperparameters; the text says intermediate dictionary dimensions seem optimal. Exact plotted scores are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Best single-feature TC probe F1 peaks at intermediate dictionary sizes (nl=2048, 4096) in GraphCast layer-8 TopK SAEs. AR probes show no clear size trend. The authors speculate that larger SAEs split TCs into region-specific features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-feature probe performance for a broad category can peak at intermediate SAE dictionary size, possibly because the category splits into finer features at larger sizes.

record.problems: The feature-splitting explanation is speculative. The relevant sweep is presented in a plot without exact scores stated in the text, and the paper does not directly compare or match features across dictionary sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No other probe or intervention results were included because they do not measure dictionary-size feature splitting or its proposed input and geometric relationships.

untested.parts: All: no cross-size feature matching, input partitioning or directional similarity.
All: GraphCast is a non-language GNN, but splitting itself is not measured.
All: no nested families or hierarchy geometry examined.
All: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller ones.

record.verdict_notes: The study's main results (sea-ice, diurnal and TC features; TC feature steering with physical-consistency checks) do not bear on splitting. Best TC F1 is 0.48 for nl=4096, k=32, versus 0.01 for neurons; these are selection or capability values, not splitting measures.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a coarse feature is replaced by more specific features that cover its inputs and lie near its direction.
Whether the pattern holds in large models or open SAE releases.
Whether split features form nested, geometrically close families reflecting a concept hierarchy.
Whether parent latents fail to fire where child latents take over, and whether size or sparsity changes fix this.
Whether larger latents decompose into smaller latents and whether larger dictionaries add novel latents.
Whether splitting is an artifact of the SAE objective or changes under alternative objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.operation_detail: Compared single-feature tropical-cyclone probe performance across SAE hyperparameter choices, including dictionary dimensions.
rows.measure: Best single-feature logistic-probe F1 score across dictionary-size choices
rows.value: The text says intermediate-sized latent layers (nl = 2048, 4096) seem optimal; exact scores are figure only.
rows.note: The authors hypothesize that feature splitting may explain the probe trend, possibly because larger SAEs learn different TC features for different regions. The probe scores do not measure feature replacement, input partitioning, or directional proximity.
rows.check: The row measures best single-feature probe F1 against a TC mask, not feature replacement, coverage or geometry. Exact values are in Figure 9 only. The text states the trend: intermediate nl=2048 and 4096 'seems optimal'. The AR sweep showed no clear trend; this belongs in the row or a note.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
